outcome: No case, bound, or resolution of the conjecture as stated has been established since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open, with a large volume of unreviewed preprints claiming resolutions and one serious strategy paper (Connes-Consani-Moscovici, Nov 2025) that stops short of a proof.
summary: The current (2026) Hilbert–Pólya conjecture Wikipedia article still describes the conjecture as unproven, with its most recent substantive entry dating to 2017 (Bender–Brody–Müller, criticized by Bellissard) — nothing in the live article postdates 26 January 2024 as a change to the conjecture's status. My own search turned up two distinct tiers of activity in the window. (1) A serious strategy paper: Connes, Consani and Moscovici, 'Zeta Spectral Triples' (arXiv:2511.22755, submitted 27 Nov 2025), constructs self-adjoint operators (rank-one perturbations of a spectral triple tied to Euler products over primes p ≤ x) whose spectra match the low-lying zeta zeros numerically with striking accuracy, and outlines a strategy for a proof via convergence of zeros as the truncation grows. The authors themselves state that 'a rigorous proof of this convergence would establish the Riemann Hypothesis' — i.e. they present a strategy and numerical evidence, not a proof, and no case of the conjecture is settled. This is genuine mathematics by credentialed authors but it does not change what the bullet's entry should say: the conjecture is still open. There is also ongoing legitimate but incomplete work by Enderalp Yakaboylu (arXiv:2408.15135, first submitted Aug 2024, revised through 2026) constructing a non-self-adjoint or conditionally-self-adjoint Hamiltonian whose reality of eigenvalues is tied to RH; it remains inconclusive and has not been digested as a resolution. (2) A large, and apparently growing, flood of self-published, non-peer-reviewed preprints on Zenodo, Preprints.org, ResearchGate, and academia.edu (checked several: Zenodo 20573045 'Proof of the Hilbert-Pólya Conjecture' by Antonio Bonelli, June 2026; Zenodo 21980608 by Michael Aksman, Aug 2026; Zenodo 21096214 by Charles Tibedo, July 2026; Preprints.org 202512.0817, Dec 2025) each independently claims to construct 'the' Hilbert-Pólya self-adjoint operator and thereby prove RH. None have any peer review, none have been digested or corroborated by a working number theorist, none appear in a journal of record, and none show any sign of being taken seriously by the mathematical community (no MathOverflow acceptance, no blog engagement from Tao or others found). None of the ones I opened mention any AI system in producing the mathematics. A separate, tangential item — a ResearchGate posting titled 'A Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis Assisted by Artificial Intelligence: An Analytic Approach' (Oct 2025) — explicitly credits ChatGPT, but its method is a direct contradiction argument on the critical strip using the zeta function's modulus, not a construction of a self-adjoint operator with the zeta zeros as its spectrum; it targets RH itself via a different route and is not scoped to this bullet's Hilbert-Pólya operator statement, and in any case is an unreviewed, almost certainly flawed self-publication (RH is unresolved). Taken together: no case or bound of the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture, as stated, has been settled in the window; the correct status is open, with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the Connes-Consani-Moscovici paper constitutes 'progress' under §6.1 as 'an instructive incident' or a bound-moving result, since it is genuine work by leading mathematicians (Connes is a Fields medalist with a long history on this exact problem) producing numerically convincing operator constructions that go further than prior attempts. However, no quantitative bound on the conjecture (which has no natural notion of a partial numeric bound — it is an existence statement about an operator) moved, and no case of the conjecture was settled: the paper is explicit that convergence to the full zero set remains conjectural. Under §3.1's rule that an existence question moves only when answered, this stays 'open' rather than 'progress'. If a future assessor believes the numerical/structural strategy itself should count as 'progress' (an instructive step, not a full case), that would be the strongest case for reclassifying; I judged it insufficient because the paper explicitly withholds claiming even a conditional resolution and it is very recent (10 months old) with no independent confirmation of its convergence claims.
what_would_settle_it: Either (a) a peer-reviewed or widely-digested proof completing the Connes-Consani-Moscovici convergence argument, which would resolve the full conjecture, or (b) any expert (e.g. Tao, a number theory blog, MathOverflow consensus) publicly engaging with one of the many self-published 'proof' preprints and confirming or refuting a specific construction — which would move the corresponding item to claimed or resolved/refuted.
